newsitem.title: FRANCE: No welcome in France for Saddam's son.
newsitem.headline: No welcome in France for Saddam's son.

text.p: France said on Sunday that Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, who was wounded in an assassination attempt last month, would not be given medical treatment on its territory.
"There is no question nor has there ever been any question that Uday should be received and treated in France," said foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt.

He was replying to queries about a report in the London-published Arabic-language newspaper al-Hayat saying Iraq wished to send Uday to France for medical treatment following the assassination attempt in Baghdad.
France, which fought against Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War, has since sought to improve its ties with the oil-rich country.
Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz is expected in Paris on Monday for talks with Prime Minister Alain Juppe and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, but not with President Jacques Chirac.
